review_comments.body: Ahh this was definitely an oversight to use `AddCleanup` like this -- since a new closure is appended each time. Good catch!

Could we possibly trigger this `Close()` in a goroutine? Docs mention that long running closes shouldn't be blocking (see [Go spec](https://go.dev/doc/gc-guide#Finalizers_cleanups_and_weak_pointers:~:text=Long%20running%20cleanups%20should%20create%20a%20goroutine%20to%20avoid%20blocking%20the%20execution%20of%20other%20cleanups%2E)).
FYI Have changed the WASM plugins to use this `wasmpool` instead

comments.body:
Thanks @gregfurman. Pushed an update: dropped `runtime.KeepAlive` and `Get()` now stops the cleanup directly; in `Put` the idle cleanup runs `Close()` in a goroutine so a slow close doesn't block. Added tests for the cleanup/cancel paths. `go test -race` passes locally.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

I was seeing some race conditions with the python processor. Ended up being some annoying issues when trying to stop the shared runtime. 

Myself + the clanker added some overengineered closing mechanism to workaround this but this component will be replaced with a Bento WASM plugin at a later stage so am not feeling sentimental about it.
